chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whenever Allah intends good for a servant, and he commits a sin, He follows it with an affliction and reminds him of seeking forgiveness; and whenever He intends evil for a servant, and he commits a sin, He follows it with a bounty to make him forget seeking forgiveness, and he continues to indulge in it.'
And this is the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'We will gradually lead them on from where they do not know.'
With the bounties during the disobedience.

key_terms.سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ: We will gradually lead them on

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between how God treats the sins of those He intends good for versus those He intends evil for?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'istidrāj' (gradual allurement), where divine blessings serve as a subtle trap to distract the sinner from repentance, whereas afflictions act as a merciful wake-up call. Rooted in Shia exegetical tradition, this mechanism highlights how God's intention—whether for ultimate salvation or continued misguidance—is revealed through the nature of the consequences following sin. It underscores the spiritual danger of comfort, which can lead to forgetfulness (ghaflah), contrasting it with the purifying effect of hardship.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from Sufyan Bin Al Simt who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Whenever Allahazwj Intends good with a servant, so (when) he commits a sin, he is followed up with by an affliction and Heazwj Reminds him of the seeking of Forgiveness; and whenever Heazwj is antagonised by a servant, so (when) he commits a sin he is followed up with a Bounty and Heazwj Lets him forget the seeking of the Forgiveness and he keeps on indulging in it; and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [7:182] And the ones who reject Our Signs, We Let them be gradually enticed from whence they know not
– with the Bounty during the disobedience’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jundab from Sufyan ibn al-Samt who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘When Allah wills good for a servant upon his committing a sin He causes it to be followed by a misfortune to remind him of the need to plead for forgiveness. When Allah wills evil for a servant upon his committing a sin He causes it to be followed by his gaining bounties that make him forget the need to plead for forgiveness and continue in sin.

This is indicated in the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘We gradually lead those who have called Our revelations mere lies, to destruction. Their destruction will be such that they will not even notice how it seized them.’ [7:182]
This happens to them by means of His granting them bounties when they commit sins.’”
